body:
Vanessa Ortiz: Dropping ADR-0142 for review/approval: provisioning orchestration model for the provision-to-ready sprint. Would love eyes from Infra + Platform + SRE. Main question: do we stay CI-driven (GitHub Actions) vs adopt a workflow engine (Temporal/Argo) vs internal service + queue.

Vanessa Ortiz: Confluence link: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/ADR-0142+-+Provisioning+Orchestration+Model

Gabe Wilson: tl;dr from the doc: proposal is an internal service (fleet-provisioner) owning the state machine + retries, emitting events, calling Terraform wrapper + image hooks + readiness gates. We intentionally *don’t* make GH Actions the source of truth.

Nina Petrova: Read through. I like that we keep the state machine in one place and use persisted transitions.

Nina Petrova: Question though: what’s the concrete reason we’re not using Argo Workflows here? We already run k8s in most envs, and it gives us a DAG + retries + UI.

Rafael Mendes: From SRE perspective: my concern with Argo/Temporal is operational surface area in week 1-2 of a sprint. We’d be on the hook for uptime + paging for the orchestrator itself.

Rafael Mendes: Also: workflow engines tend to become the “one weird place” where logs/metrics differ. If fleet-provisioner emits structured events and owns correlation IDs end-to-end, easier for oncall.

Ethan Park: +1 to central source of truth. If CI drives the workflow, we’ll end up with split-brain between “what CI thinks” vs control plane state. Control plane needs a stable Ready/Failed model.

Jordan Lee: I’m mostly looking at the audit + break-glass implications. In the internal service option, we can enforce authz + record “who paused/resumed / who overrode policy gates” in one spot.

Jordan Lee: If we push that into CI or Argo, we end up re-implementing authn/authz + auditing across systems.

Priya Natarajan: I’m aligned with the direction (service + queue). The control plane already has to reason about pool lifecycle; having the orchestrator be a real service aligns with our longer-term platform model.

Priya Natarajan: But I want to make sure we’re not quietly building Temporal-lite. ADR calls out “simple queue + workers” — what’s our cut line?

Gabe Wilson: Cut line in doc:
- No arbitrary DAG editor
- Only one pipeline shape for now (Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready/Failed)
- Explicit stage handlers with idempotency contracts
- Retry policy is bounded + backoff; no user-authored workflows
- If/when we need multi-branching, we revisit a workflow engine

Irene Choi: I’m good with “don’t introduce a new orchestrator dependency during a 4-week sprint”.

Irene Choi: We can revisit Temporal/Argo if this becomes a product/platform component across multiple workflows.

Marcus Lin: Security notes:
1) internal service makes it much easier to scope IAM narrowly (only the service role can do provisioning actions)
2) we need immutable audit logs for state transitions + break-glass.

Marcus Lin: CI-driven tends to leak creds into too many places unless we’re extremely careful.

Nina Petrova: That makes sense. My only worry is visibility/debuggability. Argo gives you a nice UI to see where you’re stuck.

Rafael Mendes: Agree on UI, but we can get 80% by:
- emitting stage start/finish/failure events
- one dashboard with per-stage timers and links to logs
- “stuck stage” alerts

Rafael Mendes: Then it’s consistent with our other ops tooling instead of a new UI.

Benji Okafor: From config validation side, I prefer the service owning the gating decision. That lets us implement:
- schema lint
- policy checks
- break-glass override (admin-only)
- automatic ticket/slack notification on override

Benji Okafor: If it’s CI, we’ll end up with “rerun the job with a magic env var” which is… not great.

Ethan Park: Also: control plane endpoints to trigger a provisioning run + query status are straightforward if the orchestrator is a service. If we go Argo, we’d be proxying Argo status through control plane anyway.

Priya Natarajan: On the “Temporal-lite” concern: I’m okay with this for now if we keep the handlers small and avoid feature creep.

Priya Natarajan: Request: can you add an explicit “non-goal: generalized workflow engine / user-authored workflows” section to ADR-0142? Helps future readers.

Vanessa Ortiz: Yep, can update ADR with that callout.

Connor O'Brien: Release/rollout angle: service + feature flag is cleaner. CI workflows are harder to stage safely (people will click buttons in prod). With a service we can control enablement per env/pool.

Nina Petrova: Another question: where do we persist state machine transitions? DB table in control plane vs separate store?

Ethan Park: ADR suggests persistence in control plane DB (same place where pool records live), with provisioning_runs + provisioning_events tables. I’m in favor — less infra.

Rafael Mendes: +1 if it means we can query it from existing tooling and correlate with routing “ready”.

Jordan Lee: If it’s in control plane DB, please ensure we include “actor” fields (service vs operator) and correlation_id. We’ll want that for audits.

Gabe Wilson: Noted. Current schema draft includes: run_id, pool_id, stage, status, started_at/finished_at, error_code, error_message (sanitized), correlation_id, initiated_by.

Marcus Lin: Sanitization: make sure error_message doesn’t accidentally include secrets (terraform outputs sometimes do weird things). Prefer structured error codes + link to logs.

Vanessa Ortiz: Good call. We’ll keep messages short + pointers.

Priya Natarajan: Okay. From Platform side: 👍 approve ADR direction (internal service + queue + persisted state machine), with the minor ADR update requested.

Irene Choi: Infra approval from me as well. Please tag me on the final ADR update.

Rafael Mendes: SRE 👍, with ask that we explicitly define retry bounds + cancellation semantics (so oncall can stop a runaway run).

Vanessa Ortiz: Got it. I’ll update ADR today with:
- explicit non-goals on workflow engine
- retry bounds + cancel/pause semantics
- security note on error sanitization

Vanessa Ortiz: Thanks all :thumbsup:
